column1: # Replaces the 61 `.diag` snapshot files, which recorded the RETIRED MoonBit
# host's rendered diagnostic (`path:L:C: type: msg` + a source excerpt + a caret
# + a `help:` line). No current code path emits that shape, no harness read
# them, and every one of them was stale -- so they could not be regenerated and
# Every fixture is compiled TWICE, and both verdicts are checked
#   * with `__no_entry__`, so a fixture with no `main` is not counted as
#     rejected without the check under test ever having run -- measured, that
#     masked 4 of the 13 lost checks below; and
#   * with `main`, the entry name a user passes, because `__no_entry__` skips
#     the entry-boundary lowering and a diagnostic raised THERE (handle
#     eligibility, ADR-0076) is invisible to the first lane.
# The corpus used to be compiled the first way only, and a row therefore
# claimed `ok` for a program `vibe check` rejects (#2142, #2144). Measured over
# all 233 rows both ways, on a stage2 built from this checkout:
#   204 rows      same verdict in both lanes
#    28 rows      no `main` to name, so there is no entry lane to compare --
#                 the entry compile stops at "entry `main` not found". This is
#                 why the corpus cannot simply switch entry names wholesale.
# A divergence must be RECORDED in the row (columns 4-5 below) or the gate
# fails, so the next one cannot be silent. Recording it is also what pins the
# entry-lane message: the eligibility boundary had no fixture coverage at all
# before, because the place fixture coverage is kept could not see it.
#   1 NAME          fixture stem, in fixtures/typecheck/ or fixtures/
#   3 NEEDLE        substring of the diagnostic, required for a rejecting row
#   4 ENTRY-STATUS  `ok` or `reject` -- present ONLY when the entry lane
#                   disagrees with column 2. An annotation that no longer
#                   diverges is an error: it would hide the next real one.
#   5 ENTRY-NEEDLE  substring of the entry lane's diagnostic
#   reject        rejected, and should -- NEEDLE must appear in the diagnostic
#   debt-accepts  compiles TODAY but should be rejected. NEEDLE is the check
#                 that has been lost, quoted from the retired snapshot.
#   debt-rejects  rejected TODAY but should compile. NEEDLE is today's message.
# The gate (scripts/compiler_gate.sh) asserts TODAY'S behaviour for every row,
# so it stays green, and fails if a `debt-*` row starts behaving as intended --
# that is the signal to promote the row, the same ratchet
# scripts/vibe_fmt_allowlist.txt uses. New fixtures must not be added as debt.
# A `debt-*` row is a claim that the RETIRED host's verdict is still the one we
# want. That claim needs checking per row before anyone "restores" the check --
# some of these rules were changed deliberately, and some describe features the
# selfhost compiler does not have. Two rows have already been re-read this way:
#     DECIDED that a fully-positional call to a `~`-labeled function is fine
#     (only MIXING labeled and positional in one call is rejected), and
#     checker_labeled_arg_test pins exactly that: "1001: fully-positional call
#     is not a mix, stays accepted". The debt row was aimed at a rule the
#     project had already moved off on purpose.
#   scoped_ref_param_{,nested_}decl_forbidden  now `reject`, but NOT for the
#     recorded reason. `Ref[T]` does not exist in the selfhost compiler -- no
#     such builtin type, no use anywhere in lib/. These fixtures used to
#     compile because an UNRESOLVED type name in a signature was accepted at
#     all. #2125 made that a diagnostic, so they are rejected as "unknown type
#     `Ref`" -- name resolution in type position, not Ref escape analysis. Do
#     not "restore" a Ref escape check to close these.
#     retired host could not do polymorphic recursion; the selfhost compiler
#     can. Verified by RUNNING it, not just compiling it:
#       let rec depth = [T](x: T, n: Int) -> Int {
#     "Restoring" this rejection would remove a capability the compiler has.
#     reclassified `reject`. There is NO `Error` trait in the selfhost compiler
#     -- `[E: Error]` names an undefined trait, and rejecting it is right.
#     ADR-0085 replaced the trait-bound design: the exception kind rides the
#     ROW (`Exception[E]`), not a bound on the payload type. (The diagnostic
#     could be clearer -- "no impl `Error` for `AppError`" reads as a missing
#     impl rather than an unknown trait -- but that is separate work.)
#   suberror_raise_non_error_type  still debt-accepts, same root cause: with no
#     `Error` trait there is nothing to bound a throw's payload with. Whether
#     throws are bounded AT ALL is an open ADR-0085 question, not a lost check
#     were the only GENUINE lost checks left, and worse than the fixtures
#     suggested: the leak was not about `Error` being row-transparent (that
#     hypothesis was tested and is wrong -- a capability or a user effect leaked
#     identically), so a function whose generic effect variable instantiated to
#     a CAPABILITY could claim a pure row. Fixed in #1485 by call-site
#     effect-row unification; both rows are now `reject`.

column1: # --- adopted from fixtures/ after a mechanical rewrite (#1571) -------------
# 44 more of the 139 were rejected before reaching their own check: ADR-0069
# made a top-level expression illegal, and these were written as one. Wrapping
# the trailing expression in `fn main` turned 32 of them into the specific
# diagnostic the fixture was named for -- `err_type_record_unknown_field` now
# says "unknown field 'z' on record { x: Int, y: Int }" where it used to say
# only that a top-level expression is not allowed.
# 6 compile, and are `debt-accepts`: `x += "hello"` on an Int, `apply(add, 42)`
# where `apply` wants a 1-argument function, `m[42] = 2` on a Map[String, Int],
# `type T = T`, an inline `[T](x: T: Show)` bound, and `return` inside a
# suspending loop (#1536). 3 are `ok` on purpose: two index-out-of-range
# fixtures assert a RUNTIME error the type system never promised (their own
# comments say "(runtime error)"), and untyped recursion is allowed today.
# The two Int-literal fixtures were rewritten a second time: #1877 widened the
# bound to 2^62-1, so the values they used had become legal, and they were
# asserting an overflow that no longer happened.
